title: Rigoletto
subtitle: Nucci, Swenson, Leech · Santi
summary: Off-air recording of the Metropolitan Opera's live Texaco-Metropolitan Opera Saturday matinee broadcast of Verdi's Rigoletto on March 7, 1992 (Met performance no. 682). Leo Nucci sings Rigoletto, Ruth Ann Swenson Gilda and Richard Leech the Duke; Nello Santi conducts. The 16 files (about 117 min) seem to hold only the opera, without the intermission features.
date_evidence: The folder name '920307' means 1992-03-07, a Saturday. The MetOpera Database record (CID 307650) gives 'Rigoletto (682), Metropolitan Opera House, Sat, March 7, 1992, Matinee Broadcast'. It is the only performance flagged as broadcast among the twelve Rigolettos of the 1991-92 run (nos. 677-688, Feb 17 to Mar 28, 1992). The NYPL Rodgers and Hammerstein Archives record of the Met's own broadcast tapes says 'Live broadcast from the Metropolitan Opera House, New York City, Mar. 7, 1992.' The broadcast was live, so the broadcast and performance dates are the same.
broadcaster: Texaco-Metropolitan Opera International Radio Network (the local station the collector recorded from is unknown)
event_name: Met Opera Saturday matinee broadcast (Texaco-Metropolitan Opera radio broadcast), 1991-92 season

program.title: Rigoletto
program.notes: Opera in three acts, sung in Italian, to a libretto by Francesco Maria Piave. Otto Schenk production (new in 1989).

credits.notes: This is where a substitution would show. Matteo Manuguerra sang Rigoletto at the Feb 17, 1992 run opener (s3), but both date-specific sources for March 7 name Nucci: the Met record (s1) and the NYPL broadcast-tape record (s2).
The NYPL record lists him as 'Held, Alan, 1959-'. Wikidata Q42303126 is labelled 'Alan Held' and has no English description; the Claude researcher matched it on the 1959 birth year.
Constance Green sang the Page on Feb 17, 1992 (s3). Both March 7 sources name Philley.

The March 7 Met record does not name the orchestra. The Met's house orchestra plays every Met performance, and Operadis (s4) names the 'Metropolitan Opera' orchestra for what it calls this apparent broadcast.
Not named on the March 7 Met record. Inferred because the house chorus sings every Met performance; Operadis (s4) names the 'Metropolitan Opera' chorus.

The NYPL record lists 'Allen, Peter, 1920-2016, commentator'. Its contents give him the introduction, act synopses and closing remarks. He was the broadcast's announcer, but the files may not include his segments (see open questions). No Wikidata QID, because 'Peter Allen' resolves to a disambiguation page.

open_questions: The track contents are inferred only from durations and order; nobody has listened to the files. The two researchers disagreed on tracks A5-A7 and A10-B6. The merged map uses Codex's reading for A5-A7 and Claude's for A9-B6, because those give plausible act lengths: Act 1 about 56 min, Act 2 about 28 min, Act 3 about 32 min. Check by listening: does A6 hold 'Addio, addio' or the 'Gualtier Maldè' recitative? Does A10 end after 'Cortigiani'? Does B3 hold 'La donna è mobile'?

The files total about 117 min. The NYPL copy gives 2:11:41 for the opera and a further 0:52:12 for synopses and features. The roughly 15-minute gap is probably announcer act introductions, applause and pauses between scenes edited out, but missing music has not been ruled out. Is any of Peter Allen's commentary in the files?
The A/B split (A about 72.6 min, B about 44.5 min) looks like two tape sides or two recording sessions, with B starting partway through Act 2. Was any music lost at the side change?
The local station the collector recorded from is unknown (for example WQXR in New York).
The March 7 Met record lists no production credits. The Schenk, Thomas and Wechsler credits come from the Feb 17, 1992 record of the same run.

No review of the March 7 performance and no broadcast-day station listing was found. The Opera News broadcast listing (v. 56, no. 12, Feb. 29, 1992) was not read online. No evidence of a cast change for March 7 was found: the Met record and the NYPL record of the Met's broadcast tapes agree on every role.
The Met Opera on Demand catalog PDF (s6) that Codex cited now returns 404 and has no Wayback copy, so it could not be re-checked. It is not needed for any confirmation.
